title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this part of the 'Longue Marche' continuation, Grothendieck is computing a group (here called Z̃_{ρ,σ}) of parameters μ ∈ Ẑ* (or Γ G_m) together with ν', ν'', ν_2, ν_3, subject to congruences mod 2 and mod 3. These are the data of the profinite / Teichmüller-type automorphisms acting on a configuration with SL2(Z)-type symmetry. The number N = 12 = 4·3 is presumably the order of the abelianization of SL2(Z). The previous page establishes μ = 4ν' − 2ν_2 + 1 = 6ν'' − 2ν_3 + 1, equivalently 2ν' − ν_2 = 3ν'' − ν_3.

Section 3 ('Les groupes D_N*') builds an auxiliary group scheme over S_0 = Spec Z that encodes such quantities intrinsically. The construction is as follows.
- Take the extension of discrete groups 0 → Z --N--> Z → Z/N → 0.
- Push it out along the canonical map Z → G_a.
- This gives a commutative group scheme D_N = (Z_{S_0} × G_a)/Z, where k ↦ (Nk, −k). It is an extension 0 → G_a → D_N → (Z/N)_{S_0} → 0; the 'E'' in (65) is presumably this G_a.
- Its sections are written n + N[λ], with n ∈ Z and λ ∈ Γ G_a, subject to (n + N, λ) ~ (n, λ + 1).
- Addition is (67a): (n + N[λ]) + (n' + N[λ']) = (n + n') + N[λ + λ'].

Geometrically, D_N is the disjoint union of N translates of G_a. Its extension class lies in Ext^1(Z/N, G_a) = G_a/NG_a, so it splits over Z[1/N] but not over the fibres at primes p | N. On profinite points D_N(Ẑ) ≅ Ẑ, via (n, λ) ↦ n + Nλ.

Grothendieck then claims that D_N carries a unique ring structure extending this group structure. The next page writes the multiplication as (n + N[λ])(n' + N[λ']) = nn' + N[nλ' + n'λ + (N)λλ']. So D_N is a commutative ring scheme modelling 'integers together with a congruence class mod N'. He then generalizes: for a Z-algebra A with a two-sided ideal J that is free of finite type over Z, he forms A_[N] = (A_{S_0} × J⊗G_a)/J, a ring scheme pushed out from the extension 0 → J → A → A/J → 0. The aim is to describe the parameter group of (63) as units (D_N*) of such ring schemes, with N = 12.
errors: On this page (63) reads μ = 3ν' − 2ν_2 + 1, but the previous page and the companion relation 2ν' − ν_2 = 3ν'' − ν_3 require μ = 4ν' − 2ν_2 + 1. This is either a slip of the pen or a mis-transcription.

(67b) as written ('n + N[λ] = n' + N[λ'] ⇔ n + Nλ = n' + Nλ' in Γ G_a') is not correct over a general base. The correct identification is n − n' = Nk with k ∈ Z and λ' = λ + k. For example, over Q the map (n, λ) ↦ n + Nλ has kernel much larger than the image of Z, so D_N_Q is not G_a. The criterion only works over bases such as Ẑ or Z_p with p | N, or if n ≡ n' mod N is added.

Next page (68): for the multiplication to be well defined on equivalence classes, the last term in the bracket must be Nλλ', not λλ'. Checking the change (n, λ) → (n + N, λ − 1) shows the defect is (N − c)λ', which forces c = N. This may be a transcription issue.

ideas.what: Group scheme D_N over Spec Z obtained by pushing out the discrete extension 0→Z→Z→Z/N→0 along Z→G_a; extension of constant Z/N by G_a
ideas.modern_name: pushout extension; element of Ext^1(Z/N, G_a) = G_a/N
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (SGA3-style constructions of group schemes from discrete data)

ideas.what: Ring-scheme structure on D_N, with sections n + N[λ], modelling integers with a fixed residue mod N; D_N(Ẑ) ≅ Ẑ
ideas.modern_name: affine ring scheme obtained by pushout (cf. ring schemes Z ⊕_{NZ} N·G_a)

ideas.what: Use of such ring schemes (N = 12) to encode the congruence parameters (μ, ν', ν'', ν_2, ν_3) of Teichmüller/GT-type automorphism data
ideas.modern_name: auxiliary group-scheme bookkeeping for the action of Ẑ* / GT on SL2(Z)-related objects

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up 'group schemes D_N*' (units of a ring scheme built from Z, G_a and N = 12) to package the mod-2 and mod-3 congruence parameters arising from the Teichmüller-type group. The program is not completed on this page.
missed.quote: Je dis qu'il y a dans D_N une structure d'Anneau unique, dont l'addition soit la structure de groupe déjà donnée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a scheme-theoretic, rather than purely profinite, way of encoding the congruence conditions on cyclotomic-type parameters μ ∈ Ẑ* attached to SL2(Z) (abelianization of order 12). Its value is mainly historical: it documents how he handled these computations; the mathematics itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The construction is an elementary pushout group/ring scheme with routine verifications. The only point of interest is its role in the unpublished computations of the Longue Marche continuation (N = 12 tied to SL2(Z)). No deep new result appears.
transcription_corrections: Header '673' is Grothendieck's own page number (corrected from 672).
In (63) the coefficient should likely read 4ν' (μ = 4ν' − 2ν_2 + 1), consistent with the previous page.
In (65) 'E'' is probably the additive group G_a (the kernel of D_N → Z/N), written in Grothendieck's hand.
In (66) the notation is a pushout: D_N = Z_{S_0} amalgamated with (NZ ⊗ G_a) over NZ, i.e. (Z_{S_0} × G_a)/Z.

The ring-structure sentence reads roughly: '...une structure d'Anneau unique, dont l'addition soit la structure de groupe déjà donnée, et où la multiplication induise la multiplication ensembliste [on Z]'.
